title: Fragments of Truth
next_chapter_hook: From the depths of the spatiotemporal rift came a faint sigh, its familiar frequency freezing Chen Ji in place—the fluctuations of his father's divine consciousness, he could never be mistaken.

text.content: The princess's envoy's departing silhouette vanished at the end of the Corridor, yet Chen Ji stood rooted as if struck by thunder. 'Chen Tianming is still alive'—these six words echoed ceaselessly in his mind, like violent waves crashing against the shore, shattering the calm facade he had painstakingly maintained for years. The parasol tree leaves in the courtyard rustled down, one landing precisely on his shoulder, yet he remained oblivious. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out from within the depths of the Tianji Record, carrying an unusual solemnity: 'Boy, how much do you believe of what that envoy said?' Chen Ji did not answer. His hand unconsciously moved to touch the Jade Pendant his father had left him on his chest. The moment his fingertips brushed the warm jade, a pang of bitterness shot straight from his nose to his eyes. Twelve years. He thought he had long since made peace with the fact of 'father is dead,' yet now the warmth of that Jade Pendant seared his heart with pain.

dialogue.content: 'Whether you believe it or not, what then?' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried the weariness of one who has seen through the ways of the world, 'If he truly still lives, what will you do? And if this is merely a trap, how will you respond?'

text.content: Chen Ji drew a deep breath and slowly walked back to the secret chamber. His steps appeared steady, yet if one looked closely, one would notice the knuckles gripping the Jade Pendant had already turned white. As he pushed open the stone door, he closed his eyes briefly, and when he opened them again, those pupils had regained their usual deep and tranquil calm. 'Mo Xiansheng, there is something I wish to confirm.' His voice was low, 'Whether he is dead or alive, I want to see the answer with my own eyes.' Mo Xiansheng seemed to chuckle: 'Good. That is the Chen Ji I know. However—' He paused, 'The foresight of the Tianji Record can only see events within three hours. If you wish to trace more distant threads of fate, the cost will not be small.'

dialogue.content: 'Boy, I must ask you—if he truly still lives, trapped somewhere, what will you do? Go to rescue him, or continue your chess game?'

text.content: The candle flames in the secret chamber flickered as Chen Ji sat cross-legged before the Tianji Record. His fingers gently brushed across the yellowed pages, sensing the mysterious power flowing within. For twelve years, he had used the Tianji Record to deduce the fate trajectories of countless people—from personnel changes in the three great Sects, to route maps of Demonic Path invasions, even partial layouts of the Heavenly Eye—he knew them all by heart. The only fate he had never dared to trace was his father's. 'Because I was afraid.' He finally admitted this truth, 'Afraid of seeing him alive yet being powerless to help. Even more afraid of seeing that he already has...' He did not finish, but Mo Xiansheng seemed to understand his unspoken words. The secret chamber fell into a brief silence, broken only by the occasional crackling of the candle.

'Enough, why torment yourself with so many thoughts?' Chen Ji suddenly gave a self-deprecating smile, the expression carrying a carefree air of 'what the hell.' 'I, Chen Ji, have been manipulating the world for so many years. If I cannot even confirm my own father's life or death, isn't that laughable?' With those words, he bit his fingertip, letting a drop of crimson blood fall onto the pages of the Tianji Record. Mo Xiansheng did not stop him, only saying in a heavy voice: 'Tracing fate threads consumes three times the Heavenly Fate Value of ordinary foresight, and the imagery may not be clear. Have you considered this?' Chen Ji did not answer. His consciousness had already begun sinking into that vast river of destiny, searching for that faint thread belonging to his father.

In the river of destiny, countless points of light intertwined into a web—the fate trajectories of all things in the world. Chen Ji's consciousness traversed through it, searching for that familiar frequency. After who knows how long, he finally saw it—a cluster of dim light that had been ruthlessly suppressed in a corner. Had it not been for the blood connection with Chen Tianming, it would have been nearly impossible to detect. Though the light was faint, it was clearly pulsing—tenacious and stubborn. 'Alive.' Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, pupils convulsing, 'He truly still lives!' His voice carried an uncontrollable tremor. For the first time in twelve years, this master strategist had lost his composure. Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted up: 'Don't celebrate too early. Look where your father is imprisoned.'

Chen Ji drew a deep breath and sank once more into the river of destiny. This time, he observed more carefully—that cluster of dim light was entwined by countless golden chains, each chain connected to a massive dragon-shaped phantom. 'Dragon Vein.' Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply, 'The Ancient Dragon Vein!' Mo Xiansheng's voice turned grave: 'This old man should have realized earlier... The Heavenly Eye imprisoned him at the Dragon Vein's core, using the Dragon Vein's power to suppress his cultivation and divine consciousness, making his life worse than death. This method is truly ruthless.' Chen Ji's fist slowly clenched, nails digging deep into his palm, seeping out traces of blood. 'Dragon Vein core...' He murmured the words like a prayer, 'Where is that?' Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment before giving the answer: 'The deepest part of the Imperial City's Forbidden Grounds.'

dialogue.content: 'The Imperial City's Forbidden Grounds...' Chen Ji repeated softly, his voice hoarse, 'If I recall correctly, that place is guarded by the Ancient Dragon Vein. Whoever enters uninvited—dies. Mo Xiansheng, how did my father get imprisoned there?'

'Given Chen Tianming's cultivation level, for the Heavenly Eye to imprison him there, they must have paid a considerable price.' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a contemplative tone, 'Moreover, once the Dragon Vein Guardian is activated, it will certainly alert the entire Heavenly Eye. Boy, if you insist on rescuing him, you must prepare for a direct confrontation with the Heavenly Eye.'

text.content: Chen Ji rose to his feet and slowly paced within the secret chamber. His mind raced through various pieces of information—the layout of the Imperial City's Forbidden Grounds, the triggering conditions of the Dragon Vein Guardian, the Heavenly Eye's response speed... Every variable was repeatedly calculated in his heart. After a long while, he stopped, a meaningful curve forming at the corner of his lips. 'Mo Xiansheng, I have a question.' His voice regained its usual composure, 'How long does the Dragon Vein Guardian remain active after activation?' Mo Xiansheng seemed to understand what he was thinking: 'The Dragon Vein's power is vast and boundless. Once activated, it takes at least three days to subside. During this time, anyone approaching the core will be viewed as an intruder by the Dragon Vein.' Chen Ji nodded, his eyes gleaming with brilliance: 'Three days... That will be enough.'

Just then, the Tianji Record suddenly began to tremble violently. Chen Ji's brow furrowed as he looked down to see blood-red characters appearing on the pages. The writing was twisted and eerie, emanating a chilling pressure—'Chen Ji, this One has been waiting for you.' Mo Xiansheng's voice abruptly tensed: 'This is... the Heavenly Eye's will projection! It knows you are observing!' Yet Chen Ji's expression remained unchanged; instead, he laughed lightly: 'So what if it knows? If it truly had the confidence to kill me, why resort to such psychological tactics?' With that, he reached out to wipe away the blood characters, a burning pain shooting through his fingertips. Mo Xiansheng sighed: 'Boy, you're insane.' Chen Ji replied calmly: 'For the sake of saving my father, what's one moment of madness?'

choice.prompt: Chen Ji needed to make a choice—how should he plan the operation to rescue his father?

choices.description: Infiltrate the Imperial City's Forbidden Grounds alone, without alerting anyone, and act opportunistically relying on the Tianji Record's foresight ability. The risk is highest, but if successful, the glory and prestige will be unmatched.
choices.visible_reward: If successful, monopolize all the glory of rescuing his father, and let no one know his weakness

text.content: Chen Ji shook his head, rejecting this plan. Solo action, though discreet, carried too much risk—once entangled by the Dragon Vein Guardian, there would be no one to provide backup. He was no reckless fool; he understood the importance of leaving oneself an escape route.

choices.description: Contact Ye Qing's Demonic Path forces, using her 'Demonic Path Mist' to conceal the Tianji Record's aura, while simultaneously searching for other entrances to the Imperial City's Forbidden Grounds. Medium risk, advantage lies in having backup.
choices.visible_cost: Will owe Ye Qing a favor, may expose connections with the Demonic Path
choices.visible_reward: The Demonic Path Mist can interfere with the Heavenly Eye's perception, increasing the success rate of infiltration
choices.risk_hint: The involvement of the Demonic Path forces will trigger suspicion from righteous sects, potentially affecting subsequent plans.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's voice came through the communication talisman, carrying a hint of surprise: 'Chen Ji? You're actually taking the initiative to contact me. Speak, what's the matter?' Chen Ji didn't beat around the bush, saying directly: 'I need your Demonic Path mist, and—the intelligence on the Imperial City Forbidden Grounds.' On the other end of the talisman, there was silence for a few seconds. When Ye Qing's voice rang out again, it carried a more solemn tone: 'Imperial City Forbidden Grounds... you're going there?'

choices.text: Investigate the source of the external enemy
choices.description: Before taking action, first investigate the truth of the external enemy's sudden attack—the connection between the Demonic Path commander and the Twin Fates might reveal a key to breaking the situation. The risk is lowest, but it takes the longest time.
choices.visible_cost: Delaying the rescue timing might cause the father more suffering.
choices.visible_reward: Acquire crucial intelligence and potentially discover a way to bypass the Dragon Vein guardian.

text.content: Chen Ji contemplated for a moment, deciding to first clarify the truth of the external enemy's sudden attack before making plans. His intuition told him that the connection between the Demonic Path commander and the Twin Fates was by no means coincidental—there might be secrets hidden behind this that even the Eye of Heavenly Mandate fears.

Just as Chen Ji was deep in thought, the Tianji Record flickered with a faint glow. Mo Xiansheng's voice emerged, tinged with gravity: 'Lad, before you make a decision, there are some things you must know. When you traced Chen Tianming's fate just now, I sensed an abnormality—apart from the seal of the Eye of Heavenly Mandate, another force was secretly protecting him.' Chen Ji's pupils slightly contracted: 'What force?' Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, then slowly said: 'That force's fluctuation is related to the legend of the Twin Fates. Lad, do you know that the so-called 'Twin Fates' refers to two people chosen by the Heavenly Mandate whose fates are intertwined, sharing prosperity and decline?' A thunderclap erupted in Chen Ji's mind—he thought of Chen Nian, the sister taken away by the Holy Sect and used as a 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'.

dialogue.content: 'Twin Fates...' Chen Ji's voice carried a bitter edge, 'Mo Xiansheng, are you saying that Father and Nian'er's fates are bound together? So after Nian'er was taken away, that's why Father was able to survive until now?'

'Exactly.' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried the weight of years, 'When Chen Nian was taken away, those who took her must have sensed this connection. But they didn't kill her—instead, they cultivated her into a 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'—because her existence is precisely the key to maintaining Chen Tianming's life. What the Eye of Heavenly Mandate fears is not Chen Tianming, but the fate resonance of this pair of twins. If you act rashly and disturb the seal within Chen Nian, the consequences would be dire.'

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcibly suppressing the surge of emotions. After a moment, he opened them again, and his gaze had returned to its cold composure. 'So, to rescue Father, I must first find Nian'er.' His voice was low, 'Nian'er is at the core of the Eye of Heavenly Mandate... trapped in the same place as Father.' Mo Xiansheng seemed to sigh: 'Lad, you've finally understood. This move by the Eye of Heavenly Mandate is truly vicious—separating you three father and children, keeping you always second-guessing every step.' Chen Ji coldly smiled, that smile carrying a hint of madness: 'Does it think this can trap me?' He stood up, his gaze sharp as a blade, 'Then let it see how I, Chen Ji, turn this dead game into a living one.'

He took out that token once more. This time, without hesitation, he poured his Heavenly Fate power into it. Dense patterns emerged on the token's surface, those patterns writhing like living creatures, eventually汇聚成一个模糊的画面——a cage woven from golden chains, within which curled a hunched figure. That figure had once stood tall as a pine, but now was gaunt and emaciated, with disheveled gray-white hair falling over most of their face. Yet Chen Ji recognized him instantly—it was his father, Chen Tianming. Twelve years. He had finally seen his father's appearance again. Tears fell silently, but Chen Ji smiled—that smile carried tears, carried hatred, carried twelve years of suppressed longing and fury. 'Father...' his voice was barely a whisper, 'Wait for me. I'm coming to rescue you.'

Just then, the figure in that cage seemed to sense something and suddenly raised their head. It was a face weathered by hardship, yet in those turbid eyes still flickered an unyielding light—completely different from the spirited father Chen Ji remembered, yet so achingly familiar. Chen Tianming's lips slightly parted, as if speaking. Chen Ji concentrated, trying to read the meaning from his lips. 'Don't... come...' Chen Tianming's voice, though faint, clearly reached Chen Ji's ears, 'This is... a trap...' Before the words finished, the image suddenly shattered, dissolving into scattered lights. Chen Ji tightly gripped the token, his knuckles white. 'A trap?' he murmured. Mo Xiansheng's voice spoke: 'Your father seems to have sensed something. Lad, are you certain you want to continue?'

choice.prompt: Chen Tianming issued a warning, calling it a trap. How should Chen Ji choose?

choices.description: Your father's words might be a trap lure forced out of him, or a sincere warning. Either way, he cannot let Father continue suffering.
choices.visible_cost: This might fall right into the enemy's trap, resulting in heavy losses
choices.visible_reward: Rescue Father and wash away twelve years of wrongful persecution
choices.risk_hint: If it truly is a trap, I might even lose myself in it

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes. After a moment, he opened them, and those eyes were filled with resolve. 'Even if it's a trap, I must see it with my own eyes.' His voice was soft, yet carried unwavering determination, 'Twelve years. I've made him wait too long.' Mo Xiansheng was silent for a long time, finally only saying: 'Very well, this old man will go mad with you one more time.'

choices.description: Since Father issued a warning, it means the enemy is already prepared. Must change strategy and approach the target through more indirect means.
choices.visible_cost: Need more time to布局, might miss the best timing
choices.visible_reward: Reduce risk, improve success rate, and possibly turn the tables on them
choices.risk_hint: The longer we delay, the more suffering Father endures

dialogue.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. Anger and anxiety churned in his chest, but he knew—the more critical the moment, the less he could act rashly. 'Mister Mo,' his voice returned to its usual composure, 'you say Father sensed the trap, which means the enemy is already prepared. Rather than charging head-on, perhaps... we should turn their scheme against them.'

choices.text: Trace the source of the warning
choices.description: Did Father really say those words himself? Or were they forged by the enemy? Need to confirm the authenticity of this warning first.
choices.visible_cost: Consume massive Heavenly Fate to trace back
choices.visible_reward: Confirm the authenticity of intelligence, avoid being misled
choices.risk_hint: Perhaps it was just Father's rambling during a moment of confusion

text.content: Chen Ji didn't act hastily. Instead, he once more invoked the power of the Tianji Record, attempting to trace the source of that warning. If Father's words were coerced, there would certainly be anomalous fate fluctuations to track. After a moment, his brow furrowed slightly—the warning did originate from Father himself, but threaded through it was a strand of fate not belonging to him. 'Someone is interfering with him.' Chen Ji said coldly, 'Or rather... someone is speaking through his mouth.'

The candlelight flickered in the secret chamber as Chen Ji stood before the Tianji Record, his expression obscured and uncertain. In his mind, his father's hunched figure, those turbid yet stubborn eyes, and that silent 'don't come' replayed endlessly. Twelve years had passed. He thought he had long buried his emotions beneath that mask of coldness, yet now the mask shattered into pieces. 'Father...' he murmured, his voice carrying a vulnerability never seen before, 'how can I not go?' Mister Mo said nothing, simply watching him quietly. The old guardian of the chess game had witnessed far too many such scenes—affection, love, hatred; on the chessboard of fate, these were often fatal weaknesses. But Chen Ji was different. He was the inheritor chosen by Chen Xuan, the new master of the Tianji Record, and the man who could turn the tide in the most desperate of situations.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, suppressing the surging emotions. When he raised his head again, his eyes had returned to their usual composure and depth. 'Mister Mo,' his voice was low, 'I need you to check something for me—is there a flaw in the protective formation of the Imperial Forbidden Grounds?' Mister Mo pondered for a moment: 'The Dragon Vein protection is an ancient prohibition, theoretically impenetrable. But...' he paused, 'this old man once read in a fragmentary text that although the Dragon Vein's power is immense, it has one weakness—a temporal-spatial rift. That is the boundary between the Dragon Vein and the outside world, where forces are most chaotic, and also easiest to breach.' Chen Ji's eyes lit up: 'A temporal-spatial rift... that's where Father is imprisoned!' Mister Mo said: 'Correct. That is both his cage and the only entry point. The question is whether you dare to walk it.'

Chen Ji didn't answer. His gaze fell on the final page of the Tianji Record. There was a passage he had deliberately ignored, yet now it seemed to glow faintly—'What Heaven decrees, to reverse brings death, to follow brings prosperity, only the heart remains unchanged.' These were the final words Chen Xuan left before his death. He had never understood their meaning, but suddenly gained a new insight. 'Mister Mo,' his voice was soft, 'why didn't the Eye of Heavenly Secrets simply kill my father, but imprison him for twelve years?' Mister Mo was silent for a moment: 'Because there is something it needs from Chen Tianming—perhaps his bloodline, perhaps his memories, perhaps... the other half of the Tianji Record's inheritance.' Chen Ji nodded: 'So it cannot kill him, yet hates that he doesn't die. It needs my father alive, yet wants him to suffer in agony.' A cold smile curved his lips, 'Then it certainly didn't expect his son would come to rescue him.'

dialogue.content: 'Young man, what are you planning to do?' Mister Mo's voice carried a hint of curiosity, 'This old man has followed you for so many years, yet this is the first time I've seen you risk so much for one person.'

text.content: Chen Ji didn't answer. He simply took out a jade talisman from his breast pocket. It was a hidden piece he had arranged long ago, originally intended for dealing with Ling Yuan later, but now it had found a new purpose. 'Setting the board.' he said lightly, 'Since the Eye of Heavenly Secrets wants to use my father as bait, I'll give it a classic case of 'invite the guest in only to trap them inside.' Saying this, he quickly wrote several lines on the Tianji Record. Those words transformed into flowing light and vanished into the pages. 'Ye Qing, Ling Yuan, Han Lie...' his voice was soft, yet carried a chilling intent, 'each of these people has their use.' Mister Mo seemed to understand: 'You want to use them as chess pieces, to buy you time to enter the temporal-spatial rift?' Chen Ji smiled faintly: 'Not just that.' His eyes gleamed with scheming light, 'I also want to make the Eye of Heavenly Secrets believe that everything is under its control.'

Just then, the Tianji Record trembled again. Chen Ji looked down to see a blurry image emerging on the pages—a俯瞰 view of the Imperial Forbidden Grounds, with one location marked in bright red. 'This is...' Mister Mo's voice suddenly grew solemn, 'the location of the temporal-spatial rift! The Eye of Heavenly Secrets is showing off to you.' Chen Ji, however, didn't panic but smiled instead: 'Showing off?' His smile carried a hint of amusement, 'If it truly held the winning hand, why bother with this unnecessary move?' He reached out to touch the image, and a sharp sting traveled through his fingertips—that was the will of the Eye of Heavenly Secrets attempting to invade his consciousness. Chen Ji snorted coldly, Heavenly Fate energy gathering in his palm, forcibly repelling that will. 'It's panicked.' he murmured, 'Father is in its hands, yet it's panicked—this proves I've found the right direction.'

Chen Ji withdrew his hand, his expression gradually cooling. Twelve years of strategy, countless life-or-death moments—he had long grown accustomed to burying all emotions in the deepest parts of his heart. Yet at this moment, his father's hunched figure kept appearing before his eyes, overlapping with the记忆中 spirited image from memory. 'Father...' he murmured softly, his fingers gripping that令牌 tightly, the jade edges nearly cutting into his palm. Mister Mo watched him, rare refraining from disturbance. Some emotions need to be digested alone; some obstacles need to be overcome alone. This is the cultivation every chess player must undergo. After a long while, Chen Ji took a deep breath and raised his head. The struggle and vulnerability in those eyes had vanished, replaced by a chilling composure and determination that sent chills down the spine. 'I, Chen Ji, have been setting up strategies across the world for so many years,' his voice was soft, yet each word was clear, 'if I cannot even save my own father, then what's the point of this entire chess game?'

He stood up, tucking the Tianji Record into his breast pocket. The stone door of the secret chamber slowly opened, revealing the deep night beyond, starless and moonless. 'Time to go see those old friends.' Chen Ji stepped out of the secret chamber, his voice light, 'Ye Qing, Han Lie, Ling Yuan... and that princess.' A meaningful curve appeared at the corner of his lips, 'Since the Eye of Heavenly Secrets wants to watch a show, let's give it a show worth watching.' Mister Mo sighed lightly from within the Tianji Record: 'Young man, you're planning to use all under heaven as chess pieces.' Chen Ji didn't look back, only saying lightly: 'It's not that I want to use all under heaven as chess pieces—it's that all under heaven are inherently chess pieces.' His figure vanished into the night, leaving only a softly floating phrase echoing in the secret chamber: 'It's just that this time, the chess player has become me.'

The night wind brushed against Chen Ji's robes, bringing a chill. He stood on the tallest building of the Tianqing Sect, overlooking the连绵 houses below and the sleeping disciples. This place had once been protected by his father, yet now everything had changed. 'Father,' he murmured softly, his voice scattered by the wind, 'wait a bit longer for me. This time, your son will not disappoint you.' Just then, a faint sigh drifted from the depths of the temporal-spatial rift. That familiar frequency made Chen Ji's entire body stiffen—it was his father's spiritual consciousness fluctuation, weak yet stubborn, carrying a trace of tenderness he would never mistake. Chen Ji's eyes suddenly reddened, his fists clenching until they cracked. 'I'm coming.' he silently vowed, 'This time, no one can stop me.'
